citations.narrative:
The facility’s perimeter fence could not be fully evaluated in several areas due to dense vegetation and various
materials—including tree branches, plywood, wooden boards, carpet rolls, and fencing—stored against it.
Thick vegetation and stored objects along the perimeter fence hinder assessment of its structural integrity, obscure
potential wildlife-made holes, and provide shelter for pests like rodents. They can also act as a ladder, increasing the risk
of animal escape.
The fence must be constructed so that it protects the animals in the facility by restricting animals and unauthorized
persons from going through it or under it and having contact with the animals in the facility, and so that it can function as a
secondary containment system for the animals in the facility. It must be of sufficient distance from the outside of the
primary enclosure to prevent physical contact between animals inside the enclosure and animals or persons outside the
perimeter fence. Correct by September 27, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
